gen-dafont-hero-fs-merriweather-sans: Hero stretches wide and closed, every stroke cut to a single depth. Merriweather Sans has tall, sturdy lowercase and an e that opens clearly, so a long run of text moves along without snagging.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-poppins: Poppins reads smooth and sturdy, its curves loose from end to end. Jelly Crazies is best at wobbly, nearly sealed bowls that slow the eye, while Poppins is best at carrying tall, tidy lowercase.
gen-dafont-neon-poppins: Poppins reads smoothly, with tall, sturdy lowercase and curves that never knot at the ends. Neon does its best work glowing in tall, stamped-metal forms, leaving Poppins to carry the text.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-poppins: Outrun Future traces a constant-width outline, wide-spaced and easy to follow. What stands out is how little they compete, since Poppins keeps its sans curves loose and its lowercase tall.
gen-dafont-visitor-poppins: Nostalgic and digital, Visitor pulls gaping-mouthed letters and short ascenders over big bowls, like solder through a nozzle. Poppins brings modern, loose curves that give that mood somewhere to rest.
gen-dafont-woodgod-poppins: Vintage muscle: Woodgod cuts a wide channel into every bowl. Poppins is a modern sans whose curves and straights keep one line width, so extended reading feels smooth and uncluttered.
gen-eater-bitter: Bitter is a slab-serif with a generous lowercase eye and an s you can see straight through. Eater brings the dark menace up top, so text stays dependable below.
gen-eater-inter: Dark and aggressive, Eater spaces its letters wide with short ascenders, and its thin strokes never turn spindly. Inter gives that menace a smooth, tube-like counterweight with big, open counters.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-lexend-z: Ascenders barely clear the x-height in Love Ya Like A Sister, and its terminal tips point outward, not inward. Lexend Zetta follows with widely tracked, ribbon-like strokes, tall and friendly.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-lexend-mega: Grandstander holds its letters open instead of curling them shut, with short ascenders over a tall x-height. Lexend Mega, a sans-serif with near-capital body height, works fine at modest sizes.
